description: Agent Desktop gives any agent reliable computer use on the desktop. Built with Rust, it sees any app's real UI structure through OS accessibility trees and operates it — refs stay stable and actions stay safe to retry, instead of guessing from pixels.

summary.one_liner: A Rust CLI and C library that lets AI agents read and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux through the OS accessibility tree, using stable refs instead of pixel matching.
use_cases: Let an AI agent click, type into and check apps on the desktop
Snapshot an app's UI as JSON with element refs for scripting
Automate native desktop workflows without pixel matching
Drive desktop apps from Python via the C library
Verify UI state after each action in an agent loop
Read window, notification and clipboard state from scripts
notable: Snapshots return JSON with a ref for each actionable element; refs are tied to their snapshot and rejected when stale
Headless by default: ref actions use the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus
macOS CLI calls reuse a private command host per snapshot namespace, exiting after 15 idle minutes
Ships 60 command names, with agent skill docs built into the binary via 'skills get'
Includes C FFI library for in-process calls from Python and other languages
caveats: macOS needs Accessibility permission; Linux needs a graphical session with at-spi2-core
Linux Wayland features need extra pieces (e.g. wl-clipboard) and several features are X11 only
Four key/mouse commands (key-down, key-up, mouse-down, mouse-up) refuse to run until a daemon exists
Official Homebrew and Scoop packages are not yet available in default catalogs
